request.deadline: 18-month funding period with milestones from Q3 2026 through 2027
deliverables: Establish or host a not-for-profit entity and publish transition architecture, migration plan, and public usage dashboard in Q3 2026.
Hold a board election via on-chain voting under public rules in Q4 2026.
Move public API traffic for mainnet, preview, and preprod to the new stack and legally transfer Blockfrost IP in Q1 2027.
Open a sustainability consultation and publish a long-term model proposal in Q2-Q3 2027.
Operate the public API at minimum 99% monthly uptime with quarterly technical and budget reports during 2027.
request.recipient: Input Output Global / Blockfrost transition under Intersect-administered treasury management arrangements
request.what: Fund an 18-month transition of Blockfrost into a free, community-governed not-for-profit public API for Cardano, including operations during the transition period.

claims.claim: Blockfrost is presented as a hosted REST interface that lets developers read from and interact with Cardano without running their own infrastructure or node.
The proposal says Cardano Foundation developer ecosystem survey results show Blockfrost hosted-platform usage rose from 39.3% in 2022 to 71.5% in 2025.
The proposal says Blockfrost served 781,000 unique visitors, more than 1.84 billion API requests, almost 700 requests per second, and over 7 TB of API data last month.
The proposal says more than 50% of all Cardano transactions are submitted through Blockfrost in most epochs.
The proposal says more than 100 Icebreakers have joined the decentralized Blockfrost operator effort.
The proposal commits to transferring Blockfrost source code, trademarks, domain names, and associated assets to a governing not-for-profit entity as part of the transition.

The proposed not-for-profit governance model includes a five-seat community-approved board, with four open-source infrastructure entity seats and one community seat, preceded by a named preliminary board.
The total funding request is 9,832,979 ADA, calculated as 1,868,266 USD at 0.19 USD per ADA, allocated mainly to staffing, operations and infrastructure, and legal/accounting costs.
The proposal says any unspent post-transition infrastructure budget will be returned to the treasury and that quarterly reports will include technical data and a budget summary.

The proposal states that long-term sustainability may come from paid tiers or a vendor-backed not-for-profit model, with future profits or fees supporting the public API and potentially returning proceeds to the Cardano Treasury.

summary: The document requests 9,832,979 ADA to transition Blockfrost into a community-governed not-for-profit public API over 18 months, asserting high current adoption and critical infrastructure value while proposing governance, reporting, and sustainability mechanisms.
